secrets.title: Upgrade your Secrets Management
secrets.message: The Enterprise Edition (EE) lets you add, edit, or delete secrets directly in the UI—no instance restarts needed. Organize secrets by namespace with granular RBAC permissions, and inherit them from parent to child namespaces. EE integrates with secrets managers like HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager, and Elasticsearch. Set up dedicated backends per namespace, tenant, or instance to isolate secrets across teams, or enable read-only secrets stored in external vaults. Secrets stay encrypted at rest and in transit. Optional caching reduces API calls, and audit trails log all access.

add_env.first: Encode the secret value in Base64
add_env.second: Set an environment variable named SECRET_<MY_SECRET_KEY> with the encoded value.
add_env.third: Restart your Kestra instance so the secret is loaded.

apps.title: Build custom Apps with Kestra
apps.message: Apps in Kestra Enterprise Edition allow you to build custom UIs that interact with Kestra workflows from outside the platform. This feature lets you use your workflows as a backend for custom applications, enabling non-technical users to submit data through forms or resume paused workflows awaiting approval.

blueprints.title: Start from an app blueprint.
blueprints.message: App blueprints are ready-made apps for common use cases such as forms, approvals and data submission. With Kestra Enterprise Edition, you can use any blueprint as a starting point and adapt it to build custom UIs on top of your workflows.

tests.label: Tests
tests.title: Ensure Reliability with Every Change
tests.message: Verify the logic of your flows in isolation, detect regressions early, and maintain confidence in your automations as they change and grow.

assets.label: Assets
assets.title: Bring every dataset, service, and dependency into view.
assets.message: Assets connect observability, lineage, and ownership metadata so platform teams can troubleshoot faster and deploy with confidence.

cases.label: Cases
cases.title: Triage and resolve incidents without leaving Kestra.
cases.message: Cases in Kestra Enterprise Edition let you open, assign, and track incidents directly from failed executions, with SLA tracking, activity timelines, and linked executions and assets to speed up root-cause analysis.

promote.title: Promote Flows Across Environments
promote.message: Kestra Enterprise Edition lets you promote flows from one environment to another — such as dev to staging to production — directly from the UI, no Git or CI/CD pipelines required. Review a diff of exactly what will change before promoting, protect sensitive targets with a confirmation gate, spot drift at a glance, and keep a full history of who promoted what, where, and when.

dashboards.title: Build custom dashboards tailored to your team.
dashboards.message: Custom dashboards in Kestra Enterprise Edition let you create and share your own views on top of executions, logs and metrics, combining time series, KPIs, tables and Markdown charts, with a code and no-code editor, live preview, and per-tenant default dashboards.

blueprints.title: Start from a dashboard blueprint.
blueprints.message: Dashboard blueprints are ready-made custom dashboards for common monitoring needs. With Kestra Enterprise Edition, you can use any blueprint as a starting point and adapt its charts, KPIs and tables to your team in the dashboard editor.

IAM.title: Manage Users through IAM with SSO, SCIM and RBAC
IAM.message: Kestra Enterprise Edition has built-in IAM capabilities with single sign-on (SSO), SCIM directory sync, and role-based access control (RBAC), integrating with multiple identity providers and letting you assign fine-grained permissions for users and service accounts.

tenants.title: Manage Workflows in Isolated Tenants
tenants.message: Kestra Enterprise Edition supports multi-tenancy, giving you fully isolated environments for different teams or projects, each with its own resources such as dedicated worker groups or secrets and internal storage backends.

audit-logs.title: Track Changes with Audit Logs
audit-logs.message: Kestra Enterprise Edition logs every activity with robust, immutable records, making it easy to track changes, maintain compliance, and troubleshoot issues.

quotas.title: Enforce Execution Quotas on Flows
quotas.message: Kestra Enterprise Edition lets you define quotas on flows to limit the number of concurrent or total executions within a time window. Quotas help you protect shared infrastructure, enforce SLAs, and prevent runaway workflows from consuming excessive resources.

instance.title: Manage Infrastructure Across Your Instance
instance.message: Kestra Enterprise Edition provides an operational dashboard to help you observe the health of your platform and track the uptime metrics of all services such as a.o. Workers, Schedulers, and Executors. From the same page, you can also create Announcements to notify your users about planned downtime, and you can enter a maintenance mode which temporarily puts all services and workflow executions into a paused state to perform an upgrade.

blueprints.title: Add Custom Blueprints
blueprints.message: In Kestra Enterprise Edition, you can create custom Blueprints only available to your organization. You can use them as best-practices templates to share, centralize, and document commonly used workflows in your team.

policies.label: Policies
policies.message: Policies let platform teams centrally manage and enforce rules across all flows — inject shared defaults, block plugins, bound property values, and require compliance labels. Rules apply at the tenant or namespace level with staged rollout, and every injected or replaced value stays visible to flow authors.
policies.title: Govern Every Flow with Policies

edit.title: Upgrade Your Namespace Management
edit.message: In Kestra Enterprise Edition, namespaces provide advanced isolation and governance of secrets, variables, and plugin defaults at scale. Administrators can configure custom secrets managers, isolated storage backends, dedicated worker groups, and fine-grained permissions on a per-namespace basis. This ensures that secrets, variables and plugin configurations remain secure and easy to maintain across different teams and projects.

secrets.title: Manage Secrets in a Secure Way
secrets.message: In Kestra Enterprise Edition, you can store and control secrets at the namespace level, minimizing risk and ensuring each team's credentials remain isolated. Thanks to the nested hierarchy, you can also configure credentials in a parent namespace, and they will be inherited by all child namespaces. Support for dedicated secrets managers and fine-grained namespace-level permission settings further strengthens security and compliance.

assets.title: Centralize Asset Management
assets.message: In Kestra Enterprise Edition, Assets keeps a live inventory of resources that your workflows interact with. These resources can be database tables, virtual machines, files, or any external system you work with.

variables.title: Centrally Govern Your Variables
variables.message: In Kestra Enterprise Edition, you can define and manage namespace-level variables to eliminate repetitive configurations across flows. These variables ensure consistency, simplify configuration updates, and can be easily referenced by any task or trigger for cleaner, more maintainable workflows.

policies.title: Enforce Governance Rules Across This Namespace
policies.message: In Kestra Enterprise Edition, Policies let you define rules that apply to every flow in this namespace and its children — inject shared defaults, restrict property values, block plugins, and require compliance labels, with every change fully visible to flow authors.

history.title: Manage Revision History in One Place
history.message: In Kestra Enterprise Edition, you can manage revision history of your Namespaces

audit-logs.title: Track All Changes in One Place
audit-logs.message: In Kestra Enterprise Edition, you can view namespace-level audit logs with detailed diffs, giving you a clear history of who changed what and when across all resources.

tour.menu_description: Build, run, and fix a flow, then start it from an event

actions.skipped_hint: The product tour stays in the left menu if you want to pick it up later.

intro.title: Learn Kestra in under 5 minutes
intro.body: Kestra is an orchestration platform. It makes scheduled and event-driven workflows easy to build, run, and fix.
intro.note: You can stop at any point.

copilot.title: Flows can be drafted from a prompt
copilot.body: The tour uses a ready-made example flow, so nothing has to be typed here.

flow_generated.title: This is a flow
flow_generated.body:
The flow is written in YAML with two tasks:
  1. fetch_orders to download the orders
  2. summarize to compute the revenue in Python
Tasks are executed sequentially, in the order in which they are defined.

first_execution.title: Every execution is recorded
first_execution.body: Each task is timed in the Gantt view. Clicking a task shows its logs.
first_execution.callout: Unlike a cron job or a script run by hand, every execution is kept with its inputs, outputs, and logs, so what ran can be audited afterwards.

add_task.title: Flows are edited like code
add_task.body: We added a notify task for you without the AI Copilot, so you can see what editing the YAML directly looks like. It posts the final result to Slack.
add_task.callout: A first draft from AI Copilot is only a starting point; the editor is where you iterate on it in a Code or No-Code editor tab, which both produce the same YAML, so your flow stays as code however it was built.

editor_help.title: The docs are next to the flow
editor_help.body: Documentation for the task under the cursor is shown in the Docs panel, with its properties, outputs, and examples.
editor_help.callout: Flows are built by iteration: change a property, run it, read the logs, repeat. Autocompletion and the Docs panel mean you never have to leave the editor to look something up.

failed_execution.title: A task failed
failed_execution.body: The expression for the revenue in the Slack message has a typo: vars.revenu instead of vars.revenue.
failed_execution.callout: The tasks before notify succeeded, so their outputs are still available.

fix_and_replay.title: One character changed
fix_and_replay.body: The expression is now vars.revenue. The diff shows the one line that changed, and the failed execution can be replayed from the notify task against the new revision.

replayed_execution.title: Only what failed ran again
replayed_execution.body: Outputs from the first attempt were reused, so only the notify task had to run again. This time the Slack message was sent successfully.
replayed_execution.callout: Without replay, one failed task would require rerunning the entire flow. Paid API calls would be made again, long computations repeated, and rows already written duplicated.

webhook_trigger.title: Your flow can be started by an event
webhook_trigger.body: With a Webhook trigger, this flow has its own URL. An execution is created whenever an HTTP request is sent to that URL, and the request body is available to the tasks as trigger.body.

test_event.title: Send a test event
test_event.body: The trigger is listed here. A test event can be sent from your browser, the way an external system would send it, so the trigger can be tested without leaving Kestra.

event_execution.title: The event created an execution
event_execution.body: The event arrived, and an execution was created from it, timed and logged like any other. No separate service has to be hosted for this; the trigger endpoint is part of Kestra.
event_execution.milestone: An execution you did not start

explore_payload.title: Variables, trigger, and task outputs
explore_payload.body: The Input/Output tab lists every value available to this execution.
explore_payload.callout: trigger.body is already filled in on the right. Press Debug Expression to see what it returns for this execution.

report_flow.title: One flow can depend on another
report_flow.body: daily_report has a Flow trigger, so it is started whenever order_summary succeeds. Nothing needs to be added to order_summary for that.
report_flow.callout: The two flows can be owned by different teams: daily_report declares what it waits for, and order_summary does not have to know that it exists.

chain.title: How each execution was started
chain.body: Executions you started yourself are labelled started_by:you. Others were created by the webhook event or the flow trigger.

finale.title: What you built, and what to try next

copilot.title: Flows generated from plain English
copilot.body: Describe what you want to automate in the AI Copilot chat, and a first version of the flow is generated from the live flow schema. The same is possible from your editor or terminal: Claude Code, Cursor, and other coding agents can generate flows with the Kestra agent skills.

restart.title: Replay instead of running everything again
restart.body: Task runs that already succeeded are reused, so only the work that failed has to run again, against the latest revision of the flow. Replay and restart are offered under Actions on an execution, and on a task run in the Gantt view.

events.title: Executions started by events
events.body: Webhook and Schedule triggers are part of Kestra, so an execution can be started by an event or on a schedule with nothing extra to host.

chain.title: Flows that depend on flows
chain.body: With a Flow trigger, one flow can be started by the success or failure of another flow, across namespaces. This keeps flows decoupled. Nothing in the first flow refers to the second, so both can be owned and changed independently.
